Order 
This misc. appeal u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 198 has been filed by appellants- claimants seeking enhancement of compensation amount by taking exception to the Award dated 09/02/2007 passed by V Additional MACT (Fast Track Court) Morena (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.262/2006, whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 1,07,000 along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimants on account of death of Mahendra Karnal in a motor accident.
2.The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. Challenging the impugned Award, it is contended on behalf of appellants that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28343 2 MA-511-2007 amount of compensation which is on lower side.

It is further submitted that at the time of accident, deceased was working in Petha Factory at Karnal on the post of Supervisor and he was aged about 24 years at the time of accident, therefore, his income must be assessed according to Minimum Wages Act but Claims Tribunal assessed income of deceased Rs. 15,000/- per annum.
Therefore, it is prayed that impugned award be set aside and just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded to the claimants.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
5. Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award as well as record of Claims Tribunal 6.
It is found that Tribunal awarded compensation in favour of appellants only assessing notional income i.e. Rs. 15,000/- per annum which is not correct in the eye of law.
Compensation amount must be assessed only on the basis of Minimum Wages Act i.e. 2330/- per month.

7. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 40% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 should be applied and 1/2 personal expenses of deceased should be deducted

8. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AM  Income Rs.2330 X 12= 2  Future Prospects@40% Rs.11,184/-

Total income Rs.39,144/-
 Dependency 1/2 Rs. 19,572/-
 Loss of Income Rs.19,572 X 18=
Other Heads:-
Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Compensation 9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs. 4,22,296/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.1,07,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 3,15,296/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs. 3,15,295/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
